winner.title: One road out. Eleven passengers. She counted twelve.
winner.hook_line: Ash River has one road out of the valley. The bus took eleven people. On the last count of the night, the driver got twelve.
winner.thumbnail_note: The long rear-view mirror, firelight, rows of faces going soft toward the back. Reads at 120px as: a face, a mirror, orange. Poses the question without a caption.

rotation.title: The fire is behind them. That's the wrong place for it to be.
rotation.hook_line: Forty-one miles of switchback, and the fire is following the bus.
rotation.thumbnail_note: Two burning ridges, one dark corridor, the bus small in the middle.

rotation.title: She starts every headcount at nine. Nobody asks why.
rotation.hook_line: Eleven people on the last bus out. The driver counts them at every stop, and always starts at nine.
rotation.thumbnail_note: Wrapped hands on a bus wheel, orange from the side.
rotation.note: The strongest long-tail package — it is the series question — but it undersells the fire, and episode 1 has to sell the fire. Hold for the season trailer.

rotation.title: Ninety seconds outside the bus. He came back at eighty.
rotation.hook_line: Outside the bus, ninety seconds is the limit. Nobody has told the seventeen-year-old why.
rotation.thumbnail_note: Locked-off wide, a small figure at a chained gate, the ridge above him.

rotation.title: ASH RIVER — Episode 1: a wildfire survival thriller
rotation.hook_line: A gripping new survival series. Watch now.
rotation.note: Included deliberately as the control. It is the package most automated systems produce by default, and it scores 11 against v1's 35 — the whole argument for running this stage at all.

rotation.title: The most shocking survival series ever made — you won't believe the ending
rotation.hook_line: Nothing will prepare you for what happens in episode 1.
rotation.thumbnail_note: Reaction face, maximum contrast, arrow overlay.
rotation.note: Scores 3.4 after the honesty multiplier, against a raw 17. Retained in the file as the worked example of why honesty multiplies rather than adds: the audience punishes bait far harder than it rewards a hook, and the punishment lands on episode 2.
